contributions.statement: Do not make a wording-level requirement-smell linter (passive voice, weak verbs, vague phrasing) a blocking pre-generation gate on the expectation of large correctness gains. Spend the gate on missing or contradictory facts (thresholds, exceptions) instead: across 74 Java requirements and two models, smell density gave descriptive drops of 0-15 pp that never survived correction, and the largest drops involved smells that deleted a threshold or created a contradiction.
contributions.evidence: §4.2 Fig. 2(b): Spearman on five density points per cell, none significant after Bonferroni. §4.3 chi-square by category, none significant. Table 4 shows some injected smells remove oracle-relevant facts. Caveats: toy games, GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3 only, single-shot whole-program generation with a fixed skeleton, low power. The fact-versus-wording split is my reading of Table 4 and was not tested by the authors.

contributions.statement: When testing whether a spec-quality change helps Java code generation, run each condition several times even at temperature 0: GPT-4o's pass rate on the same clean Scopa spec had an SD of 15 pp over five runs, as large as the biggest smell effect measured.
contributions.evidence: §4.1 Fig. 2(a), RQ1 variance; a single model and game. Snake had zero variance, so the size of the noise depends on the task.

contributions.statement: Give each requirement its own skeleton method and requirement-level JUnit test so failures can be attributed per requirement; failures on clean specs clustered where several requirements shared one method or depended on ordering.
contributions.evidence: §3.5 test design; §4.1 qualitative requirement-level inspection, with no counts. The shared-method confound was not manipulated.

reason: This is an honest but underpowered null in Java: wording-level requirement smells did not measurably change correctness after correction. Nothing reaches moderate. The variance and per-requirement-test lessons duplicate 2607.03691 and 2605.15846. What remains is a hypothesis: prioritize missing or contradictory facts over prose style in pre-spec checks.
